full_judgment: 7. The defendant bank contested the suit by filing a written statement. The case of the defendant bank, in short, is that the suit is barred by limitation and not maintainable in the form and manner. Messrs Mitali Enterprise (Defendant-3) opened on 12-10-1985 C/A No. 206 in the concerned branch of the defendant bank. The account- holder was duly introduced by another customer of the bank, namely, Mr. MA Sadeque, proprietor, Messrs KAFSCO OSMAN (defendant-5). Transactions made in the disputed C/A No. 206 from 1985 to 1990 were regular and usual. Therefore, there was no reason for the bank officials to suspect the bonafide of the account. Defendant being the collecting bank has no mechanism to compare the forged with genuine cheques a privilege enjoyed by the paying bank. As a collecting bank defendant is bound to collect the cheque presented by its customer. Therefore, the defendant is not liable to refund the money received and credited to the account of its customer. It is not correct to say that defendant did not cooperate with the plaintiff in disclosing the address of the account-holder and the introducer. Letters especially of 30-12-1990, 10-1-1991 and 15-4-1991 were addressed by the defendant stating its position about the address of the account-holder and the introducer. The plaintiff does not have any lawful right to claim the amount from the defendant as the defendant is not liable for the loss sustained by the plaintiff. The suit is, therefore, liable to be dismissed.
